back: F1 seed from crossing inbred lines: uniform, high-yielding; must be bought every season because saved seed gives weaker, uneven plants.
Freely pollinated cultivar; seed can be saved for a few seasons; usually lower yield potential than a hybrid.
10,000 ÷ (row spacing in m × in-row spacing in m) × plants per station.
notes: 90 cm × 30 cm, one plant per station: about 37,000 plants/ha.

front: Typical maize seed rate and spacing
back: About 25 kg/ha; for example 90 cm × 30 cm or 75 cm × 25 cm, one plant per station.
Basal compound (e.g. Compound D 7:14:7) about 300-400 kg/ha at planting; ammonium nitrate about 200-300 kg/ha top dressing, often split.
Stalk borer: windowing, dead heart, tunnels in stems. Fall armyworm: ragged holes and sawdust-like frass in the funnel.

front: Which insect spreads maize streak virus?
back: Leafhoppers. Control with resistant cultivars, early planting and removing grass weeds.

front: Sign of physiological maturity in maize
back: A black layer forms at the base of each kernel; husks dry, cobs droop, grain hard.
Dry to about 12.5% moisture, clean store, approved protectant or hermetic bags, pallets, rat-proof, inspect often.
